statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation of the multivariate Taylor expansion, as the text under 'Taylor's theorem for multivariate functions' in [wikipedia:Taylor's_theorem] is truncated after the hypothesis. As defined under 'Higher-order differentiability' in [wikipedia:Taylor's_theorem], a multivariate function f: R^n -> R is differentiable at a in R^n if and only if there exists a linear functional L = df(a): R^n -> R and a function h: R^n -> R such that f(x) = f(a) + L(x - a) + h(x) ||x - a|| with lim_{x -> a} h(x) = 0, where the differential df(a) is given by df(a)(v) = (df/dx_1)(a) v_1 + ... + (df/dx_n)(a) v_n.

symbols.meaning: remainder scaling function vanishing as x approaches a

properties.property: The differential L = df(a) of f at a is uniquely defined and given by df(a)(v) = (df/dx_1)(a) v_1 + ... + (df/dx_n)(a) v_n
properties.why: Follows from differentiability of f at a

properties.property: The order of mixed higher-order partial derivatives can be changed, justifying the multi-index notation D^alpha f = d^{|alpha|} f / dx^alpha
properties.why: Clairaut's theorem applies when all k-th order partial derivatives are continuous at a

properties.property: The function f is k times differentiable at the point a
properties.why: All (k - 1)-th order partial derivatives of f exist in some neighborhood of a and are differentiable at a

assumptions.assumption: The function f: R^n -> R is differentiable at a in R^n
assumptions.breaks_when: The linear functional L does not exist or the error term does not satisfy lim_{x -> a} h(x) = 0

assumptions.assumption: All k-th order partial derivatives of f are continuous at a
assumptions.breaks_when: Mixed partial derivatives depend on the order of differentiation, violating Clairaut's theorem

assumptions.assumption: The function f is k + 1 times continuously differentiable in a closed ball B = {y in R^n : ||a - y|| <= r} for some r > 0
assumptions.breaks_when: Any partial derivative of order up to k + 1 fails to exist or is discontinuous within the ball B

failure_modes.signature: No linear functional L exists such that the remainder vanishes faster than ||x - a||
failure_modes.cause: Partial derivatives do not exist or fail to constitute a valid differential at a

failure_modes.signature: Higher-order partial derivatives depend on the order of differentiation
failure_modes.cause: Failure of continuity conditions required by Clairaut's theorem

failure_modes.signature: Taylor polynomial approximation error does not shrink or remainder term diverges
failure_modes.cause: Poles or singularities in the extension of f restrict the radius of convergence of the series (such as poles at +-i for 1/(1+x^2))

shape: expected a derivation, produced a definition
